hook: He led India to independence without violence, and inspired the world.

pages.x: Mohandas Gandhi was born in 1869 in Porbandar, in western India. He was a shy boy, frightened of the dark. At 13 he was married to Kasturba, who was 14.
In 1888 he went to London to study law. He had promised his mother he would not touch meat, wine or women, and joined the Vegetarian Society.

In 1893, working on a case in South Africa, he was thrown off a train at Pietermaritzburg for refusing to leave a first-class carriage kept for white people. Shivering in the station all night, he decided to fight injustice.
He stayed in South Africa for 21 years, leading its Indians in peaceful resistance to unjust laws, which he called satyagraha, "truth force". He was jailed again and again.
Back in India in 1915, he became the leader of the fight for independence. He gave up Western clothes for a simple homespun cloth, spun thread every day, and urged Indians to boycott British cloth.
In 1930 he walked 390 km to the sea at Dandi to make salt, breaking the British law that taxed it. Thousands joined him, and some 60,000 people were jailed.

In 1931 he went to London for talks, and had tea with King George V at Buckingham Palace wearing his simple cloth. Asked if he had been dressed enough, he joked: "The king had enough on for both of us."

In 1942 he told Britain to "Quit India", and was jailed; his wife Kasturba died in prison. India became free in 1947, but was split into India and Pakistan amid terrible killing. Gandhi fasted to stop it.
On 30 January 1948, on his way to evening prayers in Delhi, he was shot dead by a Hindu extremist. "The light has gone out of our lives," said Nehru.
Gandhi led India to independence without violence, and inspired Martin Luther King, Nelson Mandela and peaceful protest movements all over the world.
pts: Inspired Martin Luther King and Nelson Mandela
